What began as an art therapy initiative has evolved into a platform offering incarcerated artists a chance to reintegrate into society through music. 
We explore the label’s origins, the creative vision of co-founders Dione Roach, a visual artist and director, and Steve “Vidou H” Happi, a music producer and sound engineer. We also spotlight powerful artists like Jeje, Lala Badman, Sa Ngando, and D.O.X, whose music and visuals reflect raw emotion, cultural identity, and the redemptive power of art behind bars.


We discuss the stigma around mental health in Cameroon, the role of music in rehabilitation, and the importance of providing real financial support for these artists beyond social media engagement.
